record_key: web_essential::Nivaran Essential::0
title: Nivaran Essential
content: Nivaran Essential is an individual health insurance plan that protects one adult against hospitalisation expenses.

record_key: web_essential::Nivaran Essential/Eligibility::0
title: Nivaran Essential > Eligibility
content:
Entry age: 18 to 60 years.
Available to Indian residents only.
No pre-policy medical tests up to age 45 if no pre-existing disease is declared.

record_key: web_essential::Nivaran Essential/Sum insured options::0
title: Nivaran Essential > Sum insured options
content: ₹3 lakh, ₹5 lakh, ₹10 lakh or ₹25 lakh per policy year.

record_key: web_essential::Nivaran Essential/Key benefits::0
title: Nivaran Essential > Key benefits
content:
In-patient hospitalisation expenses up to the sum insured.
Pre-hospitalisation expenses for 60 days and post-hospitalisation expenses for 90 days.
All day care procedures covered.
Room rent: single private AC room for sum insured of ₹5 lakh and above; for ₹3 lakh sum insured, room rent is limited to 1% of the sum insured per day.
Road ambulance charges up to ₹3,000 per hospitalisation.
No co-payment.

record_key: web_essential::Nivaran Essential/Waiting periods::0
title: Nivaran Essential > Waiting periods
content:
Initial waiting period: 30 days from policy start (accidents covered from day one).
Pre-existing diseases: covered after 36 months of continuous coverage.
Specific illnesses such as cataract, hernia and joint replacement: covered after 24 months.

record_key: web_family_floater::Nivaran Family Floater::0
title: Nivaran Family Floater
content: Nivaran Family Floater covers your entire family under a single sum insured that any insured member can use. It is ideal for young couples and families with children.

record_key: web_family_floater::Nivaran Family Floater/Who can be covered::0
title: Nivaran Family Floater > Who can be covered
content:
Up to 2 adults (self and spouse) aged 18 to 60 years at entry.
Up to 4 dependent children aged 91 days to 25 years.
Parents are not covered under this plan. Parents aged 60 to 75 can be insured under Nivaran Senior Care.
Lifelong renewal is available once the policy is issued.

record_key: web_family_floater::Nivaran Family Floater/Sum insured options::0
title: Nivaran Family Floater > Sum insured options
content: Choose a floater sum insured of ₹5 lakh, ₹10 lakh, ₹25 lakh or ₹50 lakh. The sum insured is shared by all insured family members for the policy year.

record_key: web_family_floater::Nivaran Family Floater/Key benefits::0
title: Nivaran Family Floater > Key benefits
content:
In-patient hospitalisation expenses up to the sum insured.
Pre-hospitalisation expenses for 60 days and post-hospitalisation expenses for 90 days.
All day care procedures covered.
Single private AC room for sum insured of ₹5 lakh and above.
AYUSH treatment covered up to the sum insured.
Free annual health check-up for all insured adults after every claim-free year.
No co-payment for members below 60 years of age.

record_key: web_family_floater::Nivaran Family Floater/Maternity and newborn cover::0
title: Nivaran Family Floater > Maternity and newborn cover
content: Maternity expenses are covered only under Family Floater policies with a sum insured of ₹10 lakh or more. The benefit is ₹50,000 for a normal delivery and ₹75,000 for a caesarean delivery, after a waiting period of 24 months from the first policy start date. Newborn baby expenses are covered up to ₹25,000 from day one when maternity cover is active.

record_key: web_family_floater::Nivaran Family Floater/Waiting periods::0
title: Nivaran Family Floater > Waiting periods
content:
Initial waiting period: 30 days from policy start for all illnesses (accidents are covered from day one).
Pre-existing diseases: covered after 36 months of continuous coverage.
Specific illnesses and procedures such as cataract, hernia, kidney stones and joint replacement: covered after 24 months.

record_key: web_family_floater::Nivaran Family Floater/Optional add-on: Critical Illness Rider::0
title: Nivaran Family Floater > Optional add-on: Critical Illness Rider
content: Add the Nivaran Critical Illness Rider to receive a lump sum of ₹5 lakh to ₹25 lakh on first diagnosis of any of 20 listed critical illnesses, including cancer of specified severity, heart attack, stroke and kidney failure. Entry age for the rider is 18 to 55 years. A 90-day waiting period and a 15-day survival period apply.

title: Nivaran Senior Care
content: Nivaran Senior Care is designed for parents and senior citizens. Children can buy this policy for their parents and pay the premium on their behalf.

record_key: web_senior_care::Nivaran Senior Care/Eligibility::0
title: Nivaran Senior Care > Eligibility
content:
Entry age: 60 to 75 years. Lifelong renewal once issued.
A pre-policy medical check-up is mandatory and is arranged at the company's cost.
Individual or 2-member (husband and wife) floater options.

record_key: web_senior_care::Nivaran Senior Care/Sum insured options::0

record_key: web_senior_care::Nivaran Senior Care/Co-payment::0
title: Nivaran Senior Care > Co-payment
content: A co-payment of 20% applies to every claim under Senior Care. This means the insured pays 20% of each admissible claim amount and the company pays the remaining 80%.

record_key: web_senior_care::Nivaran Senior Care/Key benefits::0
title: Nivaran Senior Care > Key benefits
content:

Pre-hospitalisation expenses for 30 days and post-hospitalisation expenses for 60 days.
Domiciliary hospitalisation when the patient cannot be moved to a hospital.
Annual health check-up from the second policy year.

record_key: web_senior_care::Nivaran Senior Care/Waiting periods::0

Pre-existing diseases such as diabetes and hypertension: covered after 36 months.
Specific illnesses such as cataract and joint replacement: covered after 24 months.

record_key: web_faq::Frequently asked questions/What is a pre-existing disease?::0
title: Frequently asked questions > What is a pre-existing disease?
content: A pre-existing disease is any condition, ailment or injury that was diagnosed by a physician, or for which medical advice or treatment was received, within 36 months before the policy start date. Common examples are diabetes, hypertension and thyroid disorders.

record_key: web_faq::Frequently asked questions/Are pre-existing diseases covered?::0
title: Frequently asked questions > Are pre-existing diseases covered?
content: Yes. Declared pre-existing diseases are covered after a waiting period of 36 months of continuous coverage. You must declare all pre-existing diseases honestly in the proposal form; non-disclosure can lead to claim rejection or policy cancellation.

record_key: web_faq::Frequently asked questions/What is the free-look period?::0
title: Frequently asked questions > What is the free-look period?
content: You get a free-look period of 30 days from the date you receive the policy document. If you are not satisfied, you can cancel the policy during this period and receive a refund of the premium after deduction of proportionate risk premium and medical check-up costs, if any.

record_key: web_faq::Frequently asked questions/What is the grace period for renewal?::0
title: Frequently asked questions > What is the grace period for renewal?
content: The grace period is 30 days for annual, half-yearly and quarterly payment modes and 15 days for the monthly mode. Coverage continues without a break if the premium is paid within the grace period, but claims for hospitalisation during the grace period are not payable until the premium is received.

source.section: What is the grace period for renewal?

record_key: web_faq::Frequently asked questions/How does the no claim bonus work?::0
title: Frequently asked questions > How does the no claim bonus work?
content: For every claim-free policy year, the sum insured increases by 10% of the base sum insured, up to a maximum of 50%. The no claim bonus is not reduced if a claim is made later.

source.section: How does the no claim bonus work?

record_key: web_faq::Frequently asked questions/Can I get tax benefits on the premium?::0
title: Frequently asked questions > Can I get tax benefits on the premium?
content: Premiums paid for health insurance are eligible for deduction under Section 80D of the Income Tax Act, as per prevailing tax laws: up to ₹25,000 a year for self, spouse and children (₹50,000 if the eldest insured is a senior citizen), and an additional deduction for premiums paid for parents. Please consult your tax advisor for your specific situation.

source.section: Can I get tax benefits on the premium?

record_key: web_faq::Frequently asked questions/Can I pay the premium monthly?::0
title: Frequently asked questions > Can I pay the premium monthly?
content: Yes. Premiums can be paid annually, half-yearly, quarterly or monthly. Monthly payments are collected through auto-debit or UPI AutoPay mandate. A small loading applies to non-annual modes: 2% for half-yearly, 3% for quarterly and 4% for monthly.

source.section: Can I pay the premium monthly?

record_key: web_faq::Frequently asked questions/Do I need a medical test to buy a policy?::0
title: Frequently asked questions > Do I need a medical test to buy a policy?
content: No pre-policy medical tests are needed for applicants up to age 45 who do not declare any pre-existing disease. Applicants above 45 years, or applicants who declare a pre-existing disease, may need a tele-medical interview or a pre-policy health check-up. The check-up is arranged at the company's cost. Senior Care always requires a pre-policy check-up.

source.section: Do I need a medical test to buy a policy?

record_key: web_faq::Frequently asked questions/Can I port my existing health policy to Nivaran?::0
title: Frequently asked questions > Can I port my existing health policy to Nivaran?
content: Yes. You can port a health policy from another insurer at the time of renewal. Apply at least 45 days before your current policy's renewal date. Waiting periods already completed under your previous policy are credited up to the previous sum insured.

source.section: Can I port my existing health policy to Nivaran?

record_key: web_faq::Frequently asked questions/Is there any co-payment?::0
title: Frequently asked questions > Is there any co-payment?
content: There is no co-payment under Nivaran Essential and Nivaran Family Floater for members below 60 years. Nivaran Senior Care has a 20% co-payment on every claim.

record_key: web_faq::Frequently asked questions/What is not covered?::0
title: Frequently asked questions > What is not covered?
content: Major exclusions include cosmetic or plastic surgery (unless needed due to an accident or burns), dental treatment unless arising from an accident and requiring hospitalisation, spectacles and contact lenses, self-inflicted injuries, treatment for alcohol or drug abuse, experimental treatments, and expenses during the first 30 days except accidents. Refer to the policy wording for the complete list.

record_key: web_faq::Frequently asked questions/Does the policy cover COVID-19 and other infectious diseases?::0
title: Frequently asked questions > Does the policy cover COVID-19 and other infectious diseases?
content: Yes. Hospitalisation for COVID-19 and other infectious diseases is covered like any other illness, subject to the initial 30-day waiting period and policy terms.

source.section: Does the policy cover COVID-19 and other infectious diseases?

record_key: web_faq::Frequently asked questions/How do I buy a policy?::0
title: Frequently asked questions > How do I buy a policy?
content: You can buy online on our website, through a Nivaran advisor on a phone call, or at a partner branch. A licensed advisor reviews your proposal form, and the policy is issued after underwriting and premium payment. Nivaran representatives will never ask for your OTP, card PIN or net-banking password.

source.section: How do I buy a policy?

record_key: web_claims::Claims made simple/Cashless claims::0
title: Claims made simple > Cashless claims
content: Cashless treatment is available at 9,800+ network hospitals. Show your Nivaran health card or policy number at the hospital's insurance (TPA) desk. For planned hospitalisation, the hospital must send the pre-authorisation request at least 48 hours before admission. For emergency hospitalisation, the request must be sent within 24 hours of admission. Most pre-authorisation decisions are given within 1 hour, and discharge approvals within 3 hours.

record_key: web_claims::Claims made simple/Reimbursement claims::0
title: Claims made simple > Reimbursement claims
content: If you are treated at a non-network hospital, pay the bills and submit a reimbursement claim within 30 days of discharge. Required documents: claim form, discharge summary, original bills and payment receipts, investigation reports, prescriptions, and a cancelled cheque or bank details for payment. Claims are settled within 30 days of receiving the last required document.

record_key: web_claims::Claims made simple/Network hospitals::0
title: Claims made simple > Network hospitals
content: The list of network hospitals in your city is available on the Nivaran website and app under "Find a hospital". The network includes hospitals in all major Indian cities, including Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kolkata and Ahmedabad.

record_key: web_claims::Claims made simple/Grievances::0
title: Claims made simple > Grievances
content: If you are not satisfied with a claim decision, write to the grievance cell through the website or call the toll-free helpline 1800-209-4400. Grievances are acknowledged within 24 hours and resolved within 14 days. If unresolved, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman.

title: Grow with Nivaran: branch partnership > Branch partnership benefits

record_key: web_partners::Grow with Nivaran: branch partnership/Partner eligibility::0
title: Grow with Nivaran: branch partnership > Partner eligibility

content: To apply, the proposal form asks for these mandatory details: full name, date of birth, mobile number, PIN code, plan name, sum insured, number of members to be insured, pre-existing disease declaration (yes or no), nominee name and relationship, consent to be contacted. record_key: pdf_brochure_2026::Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure::0
title: Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure
content: Effective from 2026-04-01. This brochure summarises the key features of Nivaran Essential, Nivaran Family Floater, Nivaran Senior Care and the Critical Illness Rider. The policy wording prevails in case of any difference.

record_key: pdf_brochure_2026::Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure/Plan comparison::0
title: Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure > Plan comparison
content:
Entry age - Essential: 18 - 60 years; Family Floater: Adults 18 - 60, children 91 days - 25 years; Senior Care: 60 - 75 years.
Sum insured options - Essential: ₹3 lakh, 5L, 10L, 25L; Family Floater: ₹5 lakh, 10L, 25L, 50L; Senior Care: ₹3 lakh, 5L, 10L.
Co-payment - Essential: None; Family Floater: None below age 60; Senior Care: 20% on every claim.
Pre-policy medical check-up - Essential: Only above age 45 or if pre-existing disease declared; Family Floater: Only above age 45 or if pre-existing disease declared; Senior Care: Mandatory.
Renewal - Essential: Lifelong; Family Floater: Lifelong; Senior Care: Lifelong.

record_key: pdf_brochure_2026::Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure/Hospitalisation cover::0
title: Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure > Hospitalisation cover
content: All plans cover in-patient hospitalisation for a minimum of 24 hours, all day care procedures, AYUSH treatment and road ambulance charges up to ₹3,000 per hospitalisation. Pre-hospitalisation expenses are covered for 60 days and post-hospitalisation expenses for 90 days under Essential and Family Floater; Senior Care covers 30 days and 60 days respectively.

record_key: pdf_brochure_2026::Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure/Waiting periods::0
title: Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure > Waiting periods
content:
- Initial waiting period of 30 days for all illnesses except accidents.
- pre-existing disease: covered after 36 months of continuous coverage.
- Specified diseases and procedures (cataract, hernia, kidney stones, joint replacement, sinusitis): 24 months.
- Maternity (Family Floater with sum insured of ₹10 lakh or more): 24 months.

record_key: pdf_brochure_2026::Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure/Permanent exclusions::0
title: Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure > Permanent exclusions
content: The following are not covered under any Nivaran health plan: cosmetic or plastic surgery unless required due to an accident or burns; dental treatment unless arising from an accident and requiring hospitalisation; spectacles, contact lenses and hearing aids; self-inflicted injuries; treatment for alcohol or drug abuse; unproven or experimental treatments; and injuries arising from participation in hazardous or adventure sports.

record_key: pdf_brochure_2026::Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure/Critical Illness Rider::0
title: Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure > Critical Illness Rider
content: The rider pays a lump sum equal to the rider sum insured of ₹5 lakh to ₹25 lakh on first diagnosis of any of 20 listed critical illnesses. Entry age is 18 to 55 years. A waiting period of 90 days and a survival period of 15 days apply. The rider can be added at purchase or at renewal, subject to underwriting.

record_key: pdf_brochure_2026::Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure/Premium payment and discounts::0
title: Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure > Premium payment and discounts
content: Premiums can be paid annually, half-yearly, quarterly or monthly. A long-term discount of 7.5% applies for a 2-year policy and 10% for a 3-year policy paid upfront. A family discount of 10% applies when 3 or more members are covered under individual Essential policies on one proposal.

record_key: pdf_brochure_2026::Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure/Cancellation by the policyholder::0
title: Nivaran Health Plans - Product Brochure > Cancellation by the policyholder
content: The policyholder may cancel the policy at any time after the free-look period. The refund is calculated on a proportionate basis for the unexpired policy period, provided no claim has been made in the policy year.

record_key: pdf_underwriting_v4_2::Retail Health Underwriting Guidelines::0
title: Retail Health Underwriting Guidelines
content: Version 4.2, effective from 2026-04-01. These guidelines are used by advisors and underwriters to assess proposals. Advisors must not communicate a decline decision on a sales call; all non-standard cases are referred to the underwriting team.

record_key: pdf_underwriting_v4_2::Retail Health Underwriting Guidelines/Entry age::0
title: Retail Health Underwriting Guidelines > Entry age
content:
- Essential: minimum entry age 18 years, maximum entry age 60 years.
- Family Floater: adults 18 to 60 years; dependent children 91 days to 25 years.
- Senior Care: minimum entry age 60 years, maximum entry age 755 years.
- The proposer (the person paying the premium) must be at least 18 years old and need not be insured.

record_key: pdf_underwriting_v4_2::Retail Health Underwriting Guidelines/Maximum sum insured by age of eldest member::0
title: Retail Health Underwriting Guidelines > Maximum sum insured by age of eldest member
content:
18 - 45 years - Maximum sum insured: ₹50 lakh.
46 - 60 years - Maximum sum insured: ₹25 lakh.
61 - 75 years - Maximum sum insured: ₹10 lakh.

source.section: Maximum sum insured by age of eldest member

record_key: pdf_underwriting_v4_2::Retail Health Underwriting Guidelines/Medical examination requirements::0
title: Retail Health Underwriting Guidelines > Medical examination requirements
content: No medical examination is required for applicants up to 45 years without any declared pre-existing disease. Applicants aged 46 to 59, or any applicant who declares a pre-existing disease, undergo a tele-medical interview and, if required, a pre-policy check-up. All Senior Care applicants undergo a pre-policy check-up. Medical check-up costs are borne by the company.

record_key: pdf_underwriting_v4_2::Retail Health Underwriting Guidelines/Pre-existing disease underwriting::0
title: Retail Health Underwriting Guidelines > Pre-existing disease underwriting
content:
- Controlled diabetes (HbA1c below 8) or controlled hypertension: accepted with the standard 36-month pre-existing disease waiting period; a premium loading of up to 25% may apply.
- Thyroid disorders, asthma on regular medication: accepted with the standard pre-existing disease waiting period.
- History of cancer, stroke or heart surgery within the last 5 years: refer to senior underwriter.
- Kidney failure on dialysis, cirrhosis of liver, or HIV: decline.
- Body mass index above 40: refer to underwriter.

record_key: pdf_underwriting_v4_2::Retail Health Underwriting Guidelines/Residency and documentation::0
title: Retail Health Underwriting Guidelines > Residency and documentation
content: Policies are issued only to residents of India with a valid Indian address. KYC documents are collected only through the secure proposal journey, never over a voice call. PAN is mandatory when the annual premium exceeds ₹50,000.

record_key: playbook_objections::Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance)::0
title: Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance)
content: Internal guidance for advisors. Always stay factual, never promise claim approval, and never pressure the customer.

record_key: playbook_objections::Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance)/Objection: "I already have health cover from my employer"::0
title: Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance) > Objection: "I already have health cover from my employer"
content: Employer group cover usually ends when the employee leaves or changes the job, and the sum insured is often shared with the family and may be too low for a major hospitalisation. A personal policy stays with the customer for life and its waiting periods keep running from the first policy date, so pre-existing diseases get covered earlier than if the customer buys later. Suggest a personal policy as a base cover in addition to employer cover.

source.section: Objection: "I already have health cover from my employer"

record_key: playbook_objections::Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance)/Objection: "Health insurance is too expensive"::0
title: Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance) > Objection: "Health insurance is too expensive"
content: Indicative premiums start at about ₹4,200 per year for an adult aged 18 to 35 with ₹3 lakh sum insured, which is about ₹350 a month. Premiums can be paid monthly through auto-debit or UPI AutoPay. Premiums are eligible for tax deduction under Section 80D as per prevailing tax laws. The customer can start with a lower sum insured and increase it at renewal, subject to underwriting.

record_key: playbook_objections::Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance)/Objection: "I am young and healthy, I don't need it now"::0
title: Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance) > Objection: "I am young and healthy, I don't need it now"
content: Premiums are lowest when the customer is young and healthy, and no medical tests are needed up to age 45 without pre-existing diseases. The 30-day initial and 24-month specific-illness waiting periods are completed while the customer is healthy. Accidents are covered from day one.

source.section: Objection: "I am young and healthy, I don't need it now"

record_key: playbook_objections::Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance)/Objection: "Insurance companies reject claims"::0
title: Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance) > Objection: "Insurance companies reject claims"
content: Claims are paid as per the policy terms, which are shared in writing with the customer before purchase. Most claim rejections happen because of non-disclosure of pre-existing diseases or treatment during waiting periods, so encourage honest disclosure. Cashless claims at network hospitals reduce paperwork. Never promise that a claim will definitely be approved; explain the grievance process if the customer is concerned.

record_key: playbook_objections::Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance)/Objection: "I need to think about it" or "I need to discuss with my family"::0
title: Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance) > Objection: "I need to think about it" or "I need to discuss with my family"
content: Respect the decision. Offer to schedule a callback at a convenient time and to send the brochure and indicative premium details after the customer agrees to be contacted. Do not push for payment on the same call.

source.section: Objection: "I need to think about it" or "I need to discuss with my family"

record_key: playbook_objections::Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance)/Objection: "The waiting period is too long"::0
title: Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance) > Objection: "The waiting period is too long"
content: Waiting periods apply across the industry for pre-existing diseases and specific illnesses. Buying early means the waiting period ends sooner. If the customer already has a health policy with another insurer, they can port it and the completed waiting periods are credited up to the previous sum insured.

source.section: Objection: "The waiting period is too long"

record_key: playbook_objections::Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance)/Objection: "I don't trust insurance sold over the phone"::0
title: Sales Playbook: Objection Handling (Health Insurance) > Objection: "I don't trust insurance sold over the phone"
content: The customer can verify the policy details on the official Nivaran website or at a partner branch. No payment is ever taken over a voice call, and Nivaran representatives never ask for an OTP, card PIN or banking password. The policy document can be reviewed during the 30-day free-look period and cancelled if the customer is not satisfied.

source.section: Objection: "I don't trust insurance sold over the phone"
